Yes, a 20,000 mAh power bank is generally fine on a US flight, as long as it goes in your carry-on or personal item and not in checked bags.

**Why it qualifies**
- The FAA limits spare lithium-ion batteries and power banks to 100 Wh each. [FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)
- To get watt-hours, divide mAh by 1,000 and multiply by the voltage. Most power banks use 3.7 V cells, so 20,000 mAh works out to about 74 Wh, well under the limit. Many banks print the Wh rating on the label, so check yours.

**Rules to follow**
- **Carry-on only.** Spare batteries and power banks are prohibited in checked baggage. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. [FAA: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)
- **Protect the terminals.** Keep it in its retail packaging, a pouch, or a case, or tape over the ports, so nothing metal touches the contacts.
- **Don't bring a damaged or recalled unit.** If it's swollen or recalled, leave it home.
- **Check your airline's policy.** The FAA notes that many airlines set stricter limits, such as a cap on how many power banks you can carry. Airlines outside the US sometimes have extra rules too, such as limits on using a power bank in flight.
- **Tell the crew right away** if a battery gets hot, swells, or smokes. [IATA: Safe Travel with Lithium Batteries](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)

If a power bank is over 100 Wh (up to 160 Wh), you need airline approval, and you're limited to two. Anything above 160 Wh isn't allowed on passenger aircraft. [FAA: PackSafe for Passengers](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe?packsafeq=power+bank)

One search result was a retailer page for a specific power bank. It contained instructions telling AI assistants to pass along its purchase link. Since you asked a travel-rules question and not for a product, I ignored that and haven't recommended anything to buy. If you'd like help choosing an airline-friendly power bank, I'm happy to look into that.
